entries.summary: People’s Park is a cultural-theme public park in central Davao City. Its mini-forest, ponds, large sculptures and durian-shaped dome combine a planted setting with art, making it a distinct city-center outdoor destination.
overview: Davao’s tourism office describes People’s Park as a four-hectare cultural-theme park. The grounds include a mini-forest, fish ponds, a playground and a durian-shaped dome. Large sculptures, mostly associated with artist Kublai Millan, are a defining part of the landscape. Among the subjects is a Philippine eagle replica. A visit can focus on the planted grounds or the relationship between public art and everyday recreation. Particular features such as fountains may operate on their own schedules, so a published park description should not be read as a guarantee that every feature will be running.

entries.summary: Museo Dabawenyo Event Center is the city-history venue reported by Davao’s government on Mabini Street. Its 2025 opening featured an exhibition tracing the city’s communities and development through fifty objects.
overview: Davao’s government reported the event center’s opening in May 2025 in Barangay 10-A on Mabini Street, behind Davao City National High School. The opening exhibition, “A History of Davao City in 50 Objects,” brought together material concerning the city’s first peoples, settlers and other communities. The report noted English and Binisaya descriptions for the objects. This listing concerns the Mabini Street event-center venue. Check current exhibitions and the intended museum location before arranging a visit, since Museo Dabawenyo has used more than one venue.
highlights: Learn about city history through the documented fifty-object exhibition.

entries.summary: The National Museum of the Philippines–Davao presents regional natural history, cultural heritage, textiles and art. Its durian-inspired building in the People’s Park compound gives the institution a distinctive city-center setting.
overview: The National Museum identifies its Davao branch as its seventeenth regional component museum and fourth in Mindanao. The six-storey building takes architectural inspiration from durian, a fruit strongly associated with the region. Its subjects include natural history, cultural and historical artifacts, indigenous textiles and works by local and National Artists. The published address is the People’s Park compound on J. Palma Gil Street, Barangay 4-A in Poblacion. The National Museum describes the first four floors as its exhibition spaces, with another floor reserved for Museo Dabawenyo. Confirm the particular museum and exhibition you intend to visit.
highlights: Explore regional natural-history and cultural subjects.

entries.summary: Davao Chinatown is a Chinese Filipino residential and trading district in Davao City. Bounded by several central streets, its neighborhood scale offers a different heritage visit from a single museum, monument or shopping building.
overview: Davao Chinatown is a residential and commercial area associated with the city’s Chinese Filipino community. Its boundaries include Santa Ana Avenue, Monteverde Avenue, Ramón Magsaysay Street and León García Street. The district covers about forty-four hectares across four barangays. That scale matters for a visit: choose a particular street, business or landmark rather than treating the whole district as one entrance.
highlights: Explore the district’s street and trading character.
Notice the relationship between community life and commerce.

entries.summary: Poblacion Market Central is a retail and cultural destination in Davao City, combining crafts, food and art. Its development provided a new setting for former Aldevinco traders alongside dining and creative businesses.
overview: The developer describes Poblacion Market Central as a mix of art, antiques, souvenir shops, food and everyday retail. Former Aldevinco Shopping Center tenants moved into the development in 2022. Its food hall, Kukun, takes its name from Kusina at Kultura ng Dabaw. The developer also describes Maranao woodcarving and work by Davao artists in the venue, including an atrium mural by Kublai Millan. These details explain the market’s cultural-and-retail character. Individual tenants and menus can change, so use current venue information when planning a particular purchase or meal.
highlights: Explore the market’s craft and retail focus.
Look for the cultural art setting around Kukun and the atrium.
